tools.name: 1Password
tools.price_note: Teams Starter Pack about $24.95/mo flat for up to 10 members (billed annually), Business about $8.99/user/mo (billed annually), plus custom Enterprise; personal plans Individual $2.99/mo and Families $4.49/mo on annual billing, or $3.99 and $5.99 month-to-month. No free tier; 14-day free trial (re-verified 2026-08-11).

tools.name: 800.com
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-08-13, read on their own plans page with both billing tabs open) No free tier. On yearly billing: Startup $19/mo, Small Business $49/mo and Complete $99/mo; the same three month-to-month are $23, $59 and $119, badged SAVE 15%. Enterprise is quote-only. Startup covers 1,000 minutes, 1 number, 1 user and 1 extension. Small Business covers 3 numbers, 3 users and 3 extensions, with minutes listed as unlimited subject to the Fair Usage Policy. Complete covers 1,000 minutes, 5 numbers (local, toll-free or vanity), unlimited users and extensions, 1,000 transcribe minutes and 500 AI Agent minutes. Every plan carries a 30-day money-back guarantee. Listings that still name Personal, Unlimited or Pro plans are out of date.

flags.evidence: Enterprise is quote-only.

tools.name: accessiBe
tools.price_note: (2026-08-07, read on their own pricing page) Four tiers for accessWidget, priced per monthly website visits and billed yearly: Micro $490/year up to 5,000 visits a month, Growth $1,490/year up to 30,000, Scale $3,990/year up to 100,000, and Enterprise on quote above that. Micro covers automated scans and fixes every 24 hours, an accessibility statement and report, and email plus live chat. Growth adds a dedicated case manager, Google Analytics integration, multi-account and team management, and a two-day response target. Scale adds one hour with an ADA attorney, a yearly round of manual testing and validation by their experts, and custom fixes. Enterprise adds 5 to 10 attorney hours, on-demand testing, SSO and a dedicated account manager. Monthly billing exists but the page prints no monthly figures — only that paying yearly saves 30%. No free plan and no trial is listed.

flags.evidence: An overlay sits on top of a site and adjusts it in the browser.

tools.name: ActiveCampaign
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-08-17 in the browser; the figures below are the 'starts at' prices on annual billing, before you pick a contact count) No free plan, trial only. There are four tiers. Starter is from $15/mo with 1 user, limited segmentation and 5 actions per automation. Plus is from $49/mo with 1 user, standard segmentation, unlimited automation actions and landing pages. Pro is from $79/mo with 3 users, advanced segmentation, predictive and conditional content and attribution tracking. Enterprise is from $145/mo with 5 users, premium segmentation, SSO, custom objects and a dedicated account team. Your email send allowance is a multiple of your contact count — 10x on Starter and Plus, 12x on Pro, 15x on Enterprise. The bill then scales with list size: the per-contact ladder only renders after you select a contact count, which is why we could not re-verify our earlier reading of about $189/mo for Plus at 10,000 contacts on this pass. CRM pipelines, SMS and extra users remain paid add-ons.

flags.evidence: CRM pipelines, SMS and extra users remain paid add-ons.

tools.name: AdCreative.ai
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-08-15, read on their own homepage pricing table) Credit-metered, where one credit is one downloaded creative, and there is no free plan — only a 7-day trial with 10 credits. Three families, each with several credit steps. Starter is 1 user throughout: $39 a month for 10 credits and 1 brand, $89 for 15 credits and 2 brands, $139 for 30 credits and $189 for 50. Professional is 10 users and 10 brands: $249 for 50 credits, $339 for 75 and $400 for 100. Ultimate is 20 users and 25 brands: $999 for 100 credits, $1,099 for 150 and $1,399 for 200. Credits expire at the end of each billing cycle and do not roll over.

flags.evidence: (re-verified 2026-08-15, read on their own homepage pricing table) Credit-metered, where one credit is one downloaded creative, and there is no free plan — only a 7-day trial with 10 credits.

tools.name: ADP
tools.price_note: (2026-08-15, read on their own site) ADP shows no public pricing for RUN anywhere on its site, and we checked four places before saying so. /pricing returns a 404, and so does /pricing.md. The RUN product page offers only a “Get Pricing” button. And the dedicated package-comparison page lists all four tiers with “Get pricing” under each one and not a single figure. The tiers are Essential Payroll, Enhanced Payroll (adds ZipRecruiter, State Unemployment Insurance and garnishment payments), Complete Payroll & HR Plus (adds basic HR support) and HR Pro Payroll & HR (enhanced HR support and staff perks). A promotion was running when we read it: three months of free payroll, marked “Ends 8/27”, with terms behind an asterisk.

flags.evidence: The quote-only posture is normal in payroll, so the honest complaint is not that ADP hides its price — it is what that does to you as a buyer.
Ask for the per-employee-per-month rate and the per-payroll-run fee separately.

tools.name: AfterSell
tools.price_note: Tiered by monthly order volume, from about $9.99/mo up through mid tiers (roughly $34.99-$79.99) for growing stores and into higher Plus tiers (2026). Flat fees, no revenue share, with a 30-day ROI guarantee.

tools.name: AgencyAnalytics
tools.price_note: The simplified Core plan is ~$20 per client/mo with no clients included in the base — so cost scales directly with your roster (a 50-client agency pays ~$1,000/mo). Legacy plans start around $59–79/mo for 5 clients (2026).

tools.name: AgentNest
tools.price_note: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/agentnest) Four tiers, and the split between them is unusual: the diagnosis is free and you pay only for the repairs. Free: unlimited catalogue scans, a catalogue readiness score, product-level issue reports and the full findings view. Starter $19 a month: 100 successful automated fixes a month, one-click fixes for all eligible issues, product-level recommendations. Growth $49 a month: 1,000 fixes a month, revenue-priority catalogue insights, fix history and progress tracking. Scale $99 a month: 5,000 fixes a month, advanced revenue-priority insights and bulk catalogue fixes. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days, and no tier shows a free trial. The billing unit is a 'successful automated fix', and the listing never defines it. Whether one fix is one product, one field on one product, or one alt text on one image is the difference between $19 covering a hundred products and a hundred images. It is also the only variable separating the three paid tiers. Developer Ecommerce Storez, 1255 23rd St NW, Washington DC; the app launched on 6 August 2026 and has no reviews at all.

flags.evidence: On the same page Shopify shows ListingLens and StoreBeam doing the same job, also on free plans.

tools.name: AhaSlides
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Genuinely free tier: up to 50 participants and unlimited presentations, with 5 quiz and 3 unscored slides per deck. Paid plans are billed yearly and priced REGIONALLY, so there is no single figure to quote — from our test location the Essential and Pro AI tiers showed local-currency rates, and your country will see its own. What the page does state everywhere: yearly billing is advertised at up to 67% below monthly, and team licences add up to a further 20% off when several people buy together.

flags.evidence: The advertised savings assume annual commitment, and the free tier's five-quiz-slide cap nudges real quiz use toward paid.
(re-verified 2026-08-17) Genuinely free tier: up to 50 participants and unlimited presentations, with 5 quiz and 3 unscored slides per deck.

tools.name: Aira
tools.price_note: (read 2026-08-26 on aira.app/pricing) Aira is €149 per user a month, billed monthly, for the company database, AI prospecting, monitoring and on-demand research. Aira Connect starts at €499 a month, billed annually, and adds CRM enrichment and live signals on the accounts already in HubSpot, Salesforce or Pipedrive. These are euro prices for everyone: we read the page from a US connection and got the same euro figures, which fits a product that describes itself as the intelligence layer for European dealmaking across 14 markets.

tools.name: Aircall
tools.price_note: (read 2026-08-26 on aircall.io/pricing over a US connection, with their own country selector on United States) Essentials is $30 per license a month and Professional $50, both on annual billing, which the page marks as 25% off monthly. Flip that toggle and the monthly rates read $40 and $70 per license (3 licenses for $120 and $210), checked 29 August 2026 from a US connection. The discount is not uniform either: Essentials really is 25% off, but Professional lands closer to 29%, so price the plan you will actually buy rather than trusting the badge; the same cards quote 3 licenses at $90 and $150 a month. Custom starts at 25 licenses. Aircall AI is not in those numbers: voice runs from $0.19 a minute with bundles at $175 for 500 minutes and $725 for 2,500, or $0.49 a minute pay-as-you-go dropping to $0.39 above 2,500. AI conversations are $0.35 each, $0.29 after the first thousand, or bundled at $250 for 1,000 and $1,500 for 10,000. Smaller add-ons sit at $9, $10, $15, $30 and $49 per license a month, so the license fee is a floor rather than the bill.

tools.name: Airwallex
tools.price_note: (2026-08-28, read off their own pricing page and fee table; no rate below has changed since 1 Aug 2026) FX conversion 0.5% above the interbank rate for major currencies and 1% for all others. Local transfers to 120+ countries free; SWIFT transfers $15–$25 each. Payment acceptance 2.8% + $0.30 on domestic cards and 4.30% + $0.30 on international cards; local payment methods $0.30 plus method-specific fees. Corporate cards carry no international fees and up to 2% cash rebate on local USD spend. Account plans: Explore free, Grow $12 per active Spend user/month plus a platform fee that varies with team size, Accelerate custom. Their table adds limits the earlier reading did not record: the first 10 Spend users are free and the $12 rate runs to 250 Spend users; the monthly fee is charged per business legal entity, with up to 3 entities included and $1,000 per additional entity; subscription and usage-based billing cost 0.50% per successful transaction while invoicing is free; and USD balances earn a published yield of 3.21%, 3.36% and 3.48% on Explore, Grow and Accelerate. Platform API and embedded finance are quote-only.

tools.name: AISDR
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-08-17 from AiSDR's own machine-readable pricing page) There are three published plans. Solo is $250/mo or $2,400/yr for a sales team of one: 200 AI-researched contacts a month, 1 user, 1 domain, 3 mailboxes, month-to-month. Explore is $900/mo or $8,640/yr (800 contacts a month, unlimited users, 2 domains, 6 mailboxes), and Scale $2,500/mo or $24,000/yr. Annual billing takes 20% off. Explore and Scale carry a quarterly commitment; Solo runs month to month. Managed service is extra: +$149 per campaign, or fully managed from +$2,500/mo. Enterprise is custom. Priced by contact volume rather than by seat above Solo.

Business $71.99/month: 7 sites, 300 researches, 300 audit pages, 3000 SERP credits. Focus pages per account run 1 / 25 / 70 / 70. Extra SERP checker credits are $19.99 per 1,000 a month. tools.name: Algomo
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-08-17 against Algomo's own machine-readable pricing page) Plans start at $200 a month with no per-seat pricing — and that single sentence is the entire public price list. Everything beyond the starting rate sits behind a book-a-demo call, so what you actually pay depends on a conversation rather than a tier. The no-per-seat model is the part worth weighing: for a support team of any size, a flat platform fee behaves very differently from a per-agent one.

flags.evidence: Algomo is a member of the quote-only club: $200/month is the only number on the site, and the real bill for your traffic volume and feature set only emerges in a sales conversation.

tools.name: Alidrop
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Four monthly plans: Starter $39/mo (50 unique / 25 premium products), Professional $59/mo (500 unique / 250 premium), Empire $99/mo (5,000 unique / 2,500 premium) and Unicorn $299/mo (25,000 products). A 7-day trial costs $1, there are no transaction or hidden fees, and yearly billing gives up to 8 months off. An optional one-time custom-store build service is available. The $1 trial converts to the full monthly rate of whichever plan you picked, and your card stays on file — set a reminder if you are only testing.

tools.name: Alli AI
tools.price_note: (2026) 10-day free trial, cancel anytime. Business $299/mo — 5 sites, 5 team members, 500 keywords, 1,250 pages. Agency $599/mo — 15 sites, 15 team members, 2,000 keywords, 5,000 pages. Annual billing saves up to 17%.

tools.name: AltText.ai
tools.price_note: (re-verified 26 Aug 2026) Credit-metered — one credit = one image. Free trial: 25 credits, no credit card required. Monthly: Bronze $5/mo (100 credits/mo, 5¢ per image), Silver $19/mo (500), Gold $59/mo (2,000), Titanium $119/mo (5,000), Platinum $229/mo (10,000). Annual buys the same yearly credit volume at a discount the page labels 17-31% off: $49/yr (1,200 credits), $189/yr (6,000), $489/yr (24,000), $1,179/yr (60,000), $2,199/yr (120,000). One-time credit packs are 50 credits for $3 with no subscription; beyond 120,000 credits a year is custom enterprise pricing. Unused plan credits roll over when the plan renews on its normal cycle, and banked rollover credits and one-time packs stay in the account — but the FAQ states that changing plans, up or down, forfeits the current period’s unused plan credits. You can cancel anytime and keep what is unused, and every feature ships on every plan. Two multipliers change the real per-image cost: advanced formats (AVIF, HEIC, HEIF, JP2, SVG, TIFF) bill 2 credits and are paid-plans-only, and each additional translation language costs 1 more credit per image.

flags.evidence: (re-verified 26 Aug 2026) Credit-metered — one credit = one image.

tools.name: Answering Service Care
tools.price_note: (2026-08-12, read off their own pricing page, both billing toggles) Four plans, priced on included minutes. Billed monthly: Starter $40 with **zero** minutes included and $1.75 per minute after that; Small Business $179 for 100 minutes, then $1.70; Pro $329 for 250 minutes, then $1.60; Enterprise $639 for 500 minutes, then $1.35. Paying a year upfront takes about 10% off the monthly rate: $161, $296 and $575 for the three larger plans. There is also a $50 start-up fee, which appears only in the prose underneath the table and not on the plan cards. Every plan carries the same feature set: 24/7 cover, bilingual English/Spanish operators, call transfers, SMS and email relays, custom greetings and hold music, a client portal, usage reporting and the mobile app. So you are buying minutes, not capability, and there is no long-term contract. One caution about the page itself: the explanatory text below the table contradicts the table three times, quoting Pro at $319, Enterprise at $599 and Starter overage at $1.65. We have used the figures from the pricing table, which is the one the buttons act on.

tools.name: Arbor
tools.price_note: Free for households, and re-verified as such on 2026-08-17. Arbor has no pricing page at all — the URL 404s — and neither our July nor our August 2026 capture produced a figure. That is consistent with the model: Arbor is paid a referral fee by the winning electricity supplier, not by you. US-only: it works in the 13 deregulated 'energy choice' states across the Northeast, Midwest and Texas, and only on the supply portion of your bill. The delivery charges from your utility are untouched, so the saving applies to part of the bill rather than to all of it.

tools.name: AskNest
tools.price_note: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/asknest-ai-faq-product-bot) Four tiers, priced by AI replies per month, and the cheapest ladder in this category. Free: 50 AI replies a month, replies in one language you select, answers drawn from your FAQs, policy pages and product data, translated storefront widget, product finder and usage tracking. Starter $4.99 a month: 500 replies, automatic shopper-language detection across up to three languages, translated replies, product recommendations and best sellers. Growth $9.99 a month: 1,500 replies and all supported languages. Pro $19.99 a month: 5,000 replies. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days, and no paid tier shows a free trial — the free plan is the trial. What the listing never says is what happens when you run out: there is no overage rate anywhere on the page, so whether reply 501 costs money or simply does not happen is not published. 'Any language' is also not on offer; customer-facing replies and widget labels cover English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch and Brazilian Portuguese — seven. Developer Ecommerce Storez, 1255 23rd St NW, Washington DC; the app launched 8 May 2026 and has exactly one App Store review.

tools.name: Atlas AI Store Builder
tools.price_note: (prices read 2026-08-18 on apps.shopify.com/dropshipt and helloatlas.io) The listing says “Free to install”, but that is the development-store tier. A real store runs on the All-in-One plan at $39 a month, billed in USD with a 7-day free trial. Their own partners page says 5 days, so check which you get. What $39 buys is capped rather than unlimited: 5 published pages, $1,000 of bundle revenue, 250 cart orders and 50 AI photos a month. tools.name: Atria
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-08-17 on their own pricing page, annual billing, which Atria advertises as 20% off) Core is $129/mo, a stated $360 saving a year. That covers 5 seats, 4,000 AI credits a month, 50 brands followed without AI insights, 5 connected ad accounts, $500K of ad spend analysed a month, 5GB of asset storage and 3 brand profiles. Business $959/mo (a stated $2,880 saving): unlimited ad spend. Enterprise is custom. Extra seats are $20 each a month on every tier. Note the step from Core to Plus is far steeper than the tier names suggest — it is roughly 3.7x the price for 2.5x the credits.

tools.name: Aura
tools.price_note: (2026-08-28, checked line by line against their own pricing page; every figure below is the same as on 1 Aug 2026) Flat per account, not per seat, with unlimited listings on every tier. Starter $37/month ($451 a year), Essential $77 ($931), Plus $157 ($1,891), Pro $237 ($2,851) — annual saves 20%. The ladder is set by monthly sales volume, not by features: Starter up to $15K, Essential up to $50K, Plus up to $250K, Pro up to $1M. Marketplaces included: 2, 3, 4 and 6. Aura AI covers 250, 500, 1,000 and unlimited listings; Hyperdrive 10, 25, 50 and 100 allocations; user seats 1, 2, 5 and unlimited. Their table adds three things the earlier reading did not record: monthly sales are calculated on a trailing two months, workflows run 5, 10, unlimited and unlimited, and there is a 14-day free trial.

tools.name: Ava AI
tools.price_note: (verified 2026-08-28 on apps.shopify.com/ava-ai and avasales.ai) Three paid tiers, no free plan, each with a 7-day trial. Support is $29 a month and includes 100 call minutes, then $0.10 a minute; Recover is $99 a month with 400 minutes and $0.08 over; Scale is $499 a month with 1,500 minutes and $0.07 over. The headline price is really a minutes bucket: a store with real call volume pays the overage, so cost tracks conversation length, not seats. Estimate your monthly call minutes before you compare — at heavy volume the effective bill can sit well above the tier price.

tools.price_note: (2026-08-06, read in a live browser on their own pricing page, EUR view) Amazon PPC is sold in three tiers, and every one of them is a monthly fee plus an unspecified percentage of connected ad spend. They are Self Service Platform €495/month, Managed Platform €1,995/month and Managed Service €4,995/month. The tiers differ mainly in how much of a human you get. That is one monthly strategy call on Self Service, up to two calls and up to 10h of assistance a month on Managed Platform, and up to four calls and up to 32h on Managed Service. Amazon DSP is priced separately on the same page: Self Service €495/month and Managed Service €995/month, again plus a percentage of ad spend. Amazon Marketing Cloud is sold as reporting: €295 for the default report, custom reports quote-only. All prices are net with VAT added on top, and the page states that plans are based on an annual commitment paid monthly; the FAQ adds that new customers can take a paid three-month proof-of-concept period first. Walmart Managed Service, high ad-spend volumes and large agencies are contact-sales. Sellers under €10,000 a month in ad spend are pointed to a separate product, BidX Essential, whose own landing page at get.bidx.io/essentials lists $195/month for up to $10K in monthly ad spend — a flat fee with no percentage attached.

Developer Effective Apps, 13 Max Nordau, Ashdod, Israel; the app launched 7 April 2021, carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge, is available in eleven languages, and had 324 reviews at the time of writing, 5% of them one-star.

tools.name: Castmagic
tools.price_note: (read 2026-08-19 on castmagic.io/pricing) Three published tiers plus an enterprise band, and the page opens on annual billing with a 'Save 30%' label, so every headline number is the annual rate. Hobby: $19 a month billed annually, $239 a year, 30 transcribed hours, up to 3 Spaces, 50GB storage, 3 seats, no API access, no onboarding call. Starter: $48 a month billed annually, $579 a year, 100 transcribed hours, 10 Spaces, 250GB, 5 seats, API access, onboarding call. Team: $139 a month billed annually, $1,669 a year, 400 transcribed hours, 25 Spaces, 1TB, unlimited seats with 5 included and extras at $159 a year or $19 a month each, priority support. Business & Scale: from $699 a month and $999 a month, by demo, for custom volume, seats, storage, SLA and dedicated support. Unlimited AI outputs, re-generations, media clipping and audiograms are on all three published tiers, as are 60+ transcription languages, a 10GB maximum file size and the Zoom, Google Drive, Zapier, RSS and YouTube/TikTok/Instagram imports. The monthly-billing prices are behind a toggle that the page does not put in its source, so the only thing we can state about them is what the page states: annual saves 30%. And the hours need care. The table calls them 'transcribed hours (library total)' and the FAQ 'a growing library of transcribed hours that you build up over time', which never actually says whether the allowance renews each month or is a running ceiling. Extra hours can be bought at any time on every tier.

tools.name: ChatGPT AI Product Description
tools.price_note: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/automated-description-writing) Four tiers, priced in credits per month. Free Trial: 100 credits a month. Basic $19 a month or $190 a year (save 17%): 2,000 credits, product descriptions, titles and meta descriptions, formatted descriptions, automatic descriptions on import. Standard $49 a month or $399 a year (save 32%): 11,000 credits, same feature list. Pro $249 a month or $1,990 a year (save 33%): 110,000 credits, same list plus priority video-call support. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Every paid tier carries the same strapline — 'Only $1 per 100 Descriptions' — and it only holds at the bottom of the ladder: $19 for 2,000 credits is 95 cents per hundred, $49 for 11,000 is 45 cents, $249 for 110,000 is 23 cents. So the $1 is a ceiling on the cheapest plan rather than a rate, and it assumes one credit equals one description, which the listing never states. That is the central gap in this pricing: nowhere does the page say what a title, a meta description or an alt text costs in credits, or what the 'Pro Features' that use product images, metadata and web search cost extra. Developer Profitonium, Adugodi, Bangalore; the app launched 12 March 2021, holds Shopify's 'Built for Shopify' badge and carries a 4.9 average over 466 App Store reviews.

tools.name: CloudTask
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-08-19, read on their own pricing page) Two hiring models, both published, plus one deposit. A one-time $299 deposit starts your search — asked “Do you charge a monthly platform fee?” their FAQ answers “No. There is a one-time $299 deposit to start your search. That is the only fee outside the models above.” — and the deposit applies toward your buyout or your first placement. Direct Hire costs 20% to 30% of first-year base salary, paid once and quoted per role, with a 6-month replacement guarantee (one replacement, same job description) and US W2 employment available. Managed Staffing is billed as one all-in monthly rate per person covering salary, compliance, payroll and support — that rate is not published, and it is the number that decides what this costs. It carries a 24-month replacement guarantee with replacements not capped, and time and activity tracking on by default, which the hire agrees to before matching and you can switch off when you post the role. Graduating a managed hire onto your own payroll is possible after six months for a one-time placement fee quoted at that moment; no amount is published. Health and equipment benefits are available on request on Managed Staffing only.

tools.name: Cloudways
tools.price_note: (read 2026-08-26 on cloudways.com/en/pricing.php, DigitalOcean tab) No free tier, but a 3-day free trial with no credit card required. Billing is hourly and post-paid, invoiced in the first week of the following month, with no annual contract — and the hourly figure is the one that decides the bill: every card divides its monthly price by 672 hours, so $0.0208 an hour is the $14 plan. The page now opens on DigitalOcean's Premium (NVMe) column, where Micro is 1GB RAM / 1 vCPU / 25GB NVMe / 1TB bandwidth at $14/month, Small 2GB / 1 vCPU / 50GB NVMe / 2TB at $28, Medium 4GB / 2 vCPU / 80GB / 4TB at $54 and Large 8GB / 4 vCPU / 160GB / 5TB at $99. Two of those have moved since July: the entry machine is now half the size for three dollars more (July's Micro was 2GB / 50GB at $11), and the 8GB plan went from $88 to $99. Switch the column to Standard and that same 2GB / 50GB box reads $11 a month — but the hourly figure printed underneath it, $0.0357, works out to $24 at the 672-hour month the other cards use, so the two numbers on that one card cannot both be right; read the live estimate before you commit. Bought direct from DigitalOcean on the same day, an 8GB / 4 vCPU / 160GB / 5TB droplet lists at $0.07143 an hour, $48 a month. Add-ons are monthly and separate: Cloudflare Enterprise CDN from $4.99 per domain, Site Manager from $3 per app, Malware Protection from $4 per app, Rackspace email $1 per mailbox, DNS Made Easy $0.50 per domain, offsite backup storage $0.033 per GB. Advance Support is $100/month or 10% of your invoice, whichever is higher, with a limited-time flat rate of $25/month advertised on the page today; the $500 Premium Support tier we recorded in July is no longer listed there. Cloudways Autonomous, the separate autoscaling product, now prices at $35, $240 and $995 a month where July's page showed $99, $199 and $399, and it meters unique visits and bandwidth rather than RAM (30k visits and 100GB on Small, 70k and 200GB on Medium) with a 3-day free trial. Markups on AWS and Google Cloud still cannot be calculated because Cloudways does not publish the underlying instance types. A site-wide banner advertises 40% off for four months until 15 September 2026 — promotions move, so read the live price. US list prices, excluding tax.

tools.name: Datarails
tools.price_note:
(read 2026-08-25 on www.datarails.com/pricing) There is no public price. Datarails publishes three plans — Professional, Premium and Expert — and every one of them carries a Request Quote button where the number would be. The page frames that as a feature: “Get a custom quote tailored to your needs. Complete cost transparency, with no consultant fees—ever.”

What the page does publish is the shape of the ladder, and it is unusually explicit about what changes between tiers. The comparison table lists the same feature set on all three plans: reporting, planning, dashboards, Data Mapper, Lookups, Workflows, Submit Button, File Boxes, Filters, version control, the Datarails AI Suite, the FinanceOS AI Connector and permissions. Only two rows differ. Professional gives 1 integration and 2 users with standard support. Premium, marked most popular, gives 2 integrations and 5 users with premium support, and adds AI Storyboards, described as board decks in one click. Expert gives 3 integrations and 15 users with premium support, plus one “additional product included” — the line beyond FP&A runs to Datarails Month-End Close, Datarails Cash, Datarails Spend Control and Datarails Desk, and the page does not say which of those the extra slot may be spent on.

So the meter is seats and connected systems, not features. The page states no currency, no billing period, no minimum term and does not say whether a quote is annual, and there is no free plan, no free trial and no self-serve signup: the only entry point on every page of the site is Request Demo or Request Quote. Treat any Datarails figure you have seen quoted elsewhere as unverified — on 25 August 2026 the vendor's own pricing page contains no amount at all.

One of those unpublished terms the vendor will answer if you ask. On 31 August 2026, through its partner team, Datarails told us that customers typically commit to an annual term, that billing can run monthly across that year, that users can be added as a team grows, and that adding modules or capabilities beyond the core platform can carry an extra cost that depends on the scope of the expansion. That is the vendor's own account rather than a published rate, so it belongs in your quote in writing — but it does answer the term question the pricing page leaves open.

flags.evidence: On 31 August 2026, through its partner team, Datarails told us that customers typically commit to an annual term, that billing can run monthly across that year, that users can be added as a team grow…

tools.name: Drip
tools.price_note: (2026-08-12, read off their own pricing calculator; every rung on the slider re-verified 2026-08-22 and unchanged) One ladder, no tiers: you drag a slider to your list size and Drip prints a monthly price. 2,500 people is $39, then $49 at 3,000, $59 at 3,500, $69 at 4,000, $79 at 4,500, $89 at 5,000, $99 at 6,000, $109 at 7,000, $169 at 12,500, $369 at 25,000, $699 at 50,000, $1,299 at 110,000 and $1,949 at 175,000. Above roughly 175,000 the number disappears and the page says “Let’s chat”, so the top of the range is quote-only. The trial is 14 days and takes no card, but Drip states unlimited sends are switched off during it. Two things the ladder does not advertise. Chat support is not included at the entry price: up to 5,000 people the line reads “Email support”, and “Chat and email support” only appears from $99 (6,000 people) — their FAQ says the same in words. And “Unlimited email sends” stops being literally true as you climb. It still says unlimited at 30,000 people, but at 30,001 the same line reads “390,000 email sends”, at 50,000 “600,000”, at 110,000 “1,320,000” and at 175,000 “2,100,000” — in every case exactly twelve sends per contact per month. Every plan carries the same feature set otherwise, including up to 50 workflows and unlimited sub-accounts, so what you buy going up the ladder is list capacity, not capability.

Month to month the same tiers read $59, $79 and $99 per user; both columns sit in the page and the FAQ repeats all six numbers in words. A 7-day free trial runs without a credit card. So the 'up to 35% off' the toggle advertises is real but front-loaded: you pay a year up front to get it, and the discount shrinks as you go up the range — about 34 percent on Basic, 25 on Pro, 20 on Advanced. What each tier buys is unusually consequential here, and the page now prints the daily quotas instead of calling them 'limited': Basic sends 20 connection requests, 30 messages, 10 Sales Navigator InMails and 100 profile views a day, against 75, 100+, 30 and 200+ on Pro and Advanced. Basic is also capped at one drip campaign; unlimited campaigns and full quotas start at Pro, which adds a dedicated inbox, CSV export and the webhook and HubSpot integrations, and Advanced adds multi-team management, advanced LinkedIn protection, lead tagging, step analytics and evergreen leads. Every tier includes 100 email-finder credits a month and the top-ups are priced openly: 1,000 credits $29, 2,000 $49, 5,000 $69, 10,000 $99. One seat connects one LinkedIn account, so five reps means five seats, and ten or more seats goes through sales.

Essential is $24 for up to 1,500, adding loyalty status on the customer orders and profile pages and points in product cards. Growth is $79 for unlimited loyalty orders, with API integrations on request, white-glove onboarding and priority support. Paid plans carry a 14-day free trial. Charges are in USD and recur every 30 days. Developer Essential Apps; the app runs in twenty languages and works with Checkout, Customer accounts, Shopify POS, Shopify Flow, Judge.me, Klaviyo and Omnisend. Rating 5.0 from 438 reviews, of which 430 are five-star and one is one-star.

tools.price_note:
(read 2026-08-24 on apps.shopify.com/fast-bundle-product-bundles, listed as “FBP | Fast Bundle & Upsell App”, and on fastbundle.co/pricing) The meter here is not your catalogue, your traffic or your seats — it is the revenue your bundles themselves generate. The listing is free to install and shows four tiers. Development stores are free to install and free to run. Standard (1K) is $19 a month or $180 a year and covers up to $1,000 of monthly bundle sales. Standard (3K) is $49 a month or $468 a year for up to $3,000. Standard (10K) is $139 a month or $1,380 a year for up to $10,000. All three paid tiers carry a 7-day free trial and the same feature list: unlimited bundles, upsells and cross-sells, mix and match, volume-discount upsell, BOGO and Buy X Get Y, unlimited AI frequently-bought-together, product add-ons, 24/7 English support and the AI bundle image generator. The App Store states all charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days.

The vendor's own pricing page adds a fifth tier the listing never shows: Enterprise at $299 a month or $2,988 a year, described as limitless monthly bundle revenue, with automatic bundle detection in the cart, Shopify POS integration, minor specialised customisations, priority onboarding with an account manager and a five-minute support target against Standard's thirty. Launch gives you affiliate link tracking OR lead and deal registration — you pick one — plus marketplace access, partner payments built for B2B sales cycles, onboarding and enablement tooling, CRM integrations and their AI and MCP connector. Growth adds deeper integration support, a learning-management solution, partner challenges and incentives, MDF management and payments, and segmentation by performance or strategy. Enterprise is the only tier with full access to link tracking AND both registration motions at once, and adds custom workflows, a designated CSM with semi-annual business reviews, partner introductions and priority support. So the meter is not seats or volume as far as the page will say — it is which partner motions you are allowed to run, and the choice between tracking and registration on the entry tier is the line worth reading twice.

tools.price_note: (read 2026-08-22 on apps.shopify.com/protectmyorder, listed as “PMO: ProtectMyOrder”, and on protectmyorder.com/pricing) The two pages sell different ladders. The App Store listing shows one plan: free to install, then 19.99% of delivery protection revenue with a minimum charge of $20 per month, billed in USD, with the merchant keeping 80% of the upsell and handling all claims. The vendor's own pricing page, read the same day, shows three, all priced as a share of upsell revenue rather than a monthly fee. Standard at 19.99% is the plan the listing describes and adds a profitability guarantee, a gradual roll-out to 50% of visitors, fully customisable design and wording, and an assigned support agent. Carbon at 24.99% adds automatic carbon calculation and offsetting for every delivery, with a choice of project. Pro at 44.99% puts ProtectMyOrder's own agents on your shipping-claim support with 24/7 cover and ten-minute replies, and for a further 30% of upsell revenue they assume the liability for refunds and replacements as well — 74.99% in total. The same page offers volume discounts, by call, to brands above $20m of online revenue. The app sells protection against lost and stolen parcels, carbon-neutral shipping and free returns on the cart page, in checkout or through a custom widget, with fixed, dynamic or percentage pricing, instant quotes, custom branding and custom policies. It works with Checkout, Bundles, Klaviyo, Order Editing, Rebuy, Recharge and Stockly, is English-only, and sits in Shopify's warranties and insurance category. Developer ProtectMyOrder; the app launched 14 June 2023 and carried twelve reviews, all at the top rating, at the time of writing.

The mechanism most reviews miss is Attendee Units: AUs are attendees without a paid Reclaim seat in Smart Meetings of 3 or more people (two-person meetings do not need them), and they accumulate. Extra AUs are bought in packs on top of the seat. On Starter that is $8/month for 3, $16 for 6, $24 for 9 and $32 for 12. If you schedule across people who do not have seats, the AU packs rather than the seat price are what determines your bill. Discount codes appear on the page periodically.

tools.name: respond.io
tools.price_note: (2026-08-13, read off respond.io/pricing) Four tiers, billed on monthly active contacts rather than seats: Starter $79/month, Growth $159, Advanced $279, and Enterprise on quote. Paying yearly takes roughly 20% off — $948, $1,908 and $3,348 a year against $1,188, $2,388 and $4,188 monthly. The trial is 7 days and takes no card. What separates the tiers is not volume but capability, and the line matters: Starter buys team and custom inboxes, the mobile app, AI Prompt, AI Assist, basic reports and 2FA. **Workflows automation, broadcasts, AI Agents, advanced reports, the developer API and the Zapier and Make integrations all start at Growth.** Advanced adds multiple workspaces, SSO, webhooks, HTTP requests in workflows and phone-number masking, and although a figure is shown its button says “Talk to Sales”. The page carries a selector for 1,000 / 2,500 / 5,000 / 10,000 / more than 10,000 monthly active contacts under the heading “pay only for the contacts you talk to”, but the prices we read did not move between those settings. Ask what your contact volume actually costs before you sign — that is the meter you are buying.

tools.name: Rippling
tools.price_note: (verified 2026-08-27) Rippling is modular and mostly quote-led. The pricing page is a 'request a custom quote' form with no public numbers — you tell it which of HR, IT and Finance you need and your headcount, and a price comes back through sales. The one figure Rippling publishes is a floor: its global-payroll page advertises 'Starting at $8 per month per user' for the platform (HR, payroll, benefits, spend, devices and apps). That $8 is an entry point, not a quote — the buttons beside it read 'Get a free quote' and 'Contact Sales', and the real bill depends on which modules you switch on and how many employees you run. Some product pages show no price at all. Decide the exact module mix you need before you compare vendors, because Rippling's cost scales with how much of it you adopt.

tools.price_note: Pay-per-use GPU cloud (re-verified 2026-08-26 against runpod.io/pricing). Secure Cloud on-demand pods run from $0.27/hr (RTX A5000) and $0.49/hr (L4) up to $2.89/hr for an H100 PCIe, $3.29/hr H100 SXM, $4.59/hr H200, $6.79/hr B200 and $7.89/hr B300. Four of those moved up since July — L4 from $0.39, H100 SXM from $2.99, H200 from $4.39 and B300 from $7.39 — while the A5000 and the H100 PCIe did not move at all. The page's own structured data publishes the Community Cloud column beside every card, and that is where the real discount sits: RTX 4090 $0.34 against $0.74 on Secure, RTX 3090 $0.22 against $0.50, RTX A6000 $0.33 against $0.53, H100 PCIe $1.99 against $2.89. Serverless bills per second at a premium over pods in exchange for sub-200ms cold starts and autoscaling: $0.58/hr for the 16GB tier, $2.72/hr for an A100, $4.79/hr for an 80GB H100 (was $4.55) and $9.98/hr at the top for a B300. Storage is billed on top and is easy to miss: container disk $0.10/GB/month, volume disk $0.10 while running and $0.20 while idle, network storage $0.07/GB under 1TB and $0.05 over it, $0.14 for the high-performance tier.

tools.price_note: (read 2026-08-21 on apps.shopify.com/selixer) Three tiers, no free plan, each with a 14-day free trial. tools.name: Seller Investigators
tools.price_note: (2026-08-15, read on their own site) One number, and it is the whole model: a 25% commission, charged only after Amazon has deposited recovered funds in your account. We found it stated twice. Once on the home page — “only pay a 25% commission fee when your money is back with you” — and again in the FAQ: “no risk or upfront commitment, with a 25% recovery fee only after Amazon deposits recovered funds into your account”. The audit is free, takes 48 hours and carries no obligation. There is no subscription and no /pricing page, because there is nothing else to price. Cases they say they cover fall into five groups: inbound shipments (cancelled shipments, receiving discrepancies, carrier damage), items lost in transit or in the warehouse, items damaged or disposed of by Amazon, customer returns (refunds not returned within 60 days, overpayments, the wrong item returned, chargebacks), and overages and discrepancies (removal orders, incorrect weights or dimensions, overcharged orders); unfair reimbursement appears as a sub-case under both the lost and the damaged group. Re-read 29 August 2026: the 25% figure, the free 48-hour audit and the absence of any subscription are unchanged.

tools.name: Seller Snap
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-08-26 on their own pricing page, both the monthly and the annual column; every figure below was read again on that date and none of them had moved since 24 Jul 2026) There are four tiers, and the axis that sets your price is capacity, not features. All four list the same six feature groups: Amazon & Walmart, AI repricing technology, min & max calculation, analytics, connectivity and integrations. The four tiers are set out above; what the page does not tell you is what each step actually buys. Accelerator doubles your revenue ceiling and leaves the SKU count alone, and Standard does the reverse — fifteen times the catalogue with the ceiling removed — while the seller ID and user counts never move at all. So the middle tier is for turnover and the top tier is for range, and a shop that needs neither is paying for the other one. The revenue ceilings themselves are printed without any period attached; Seller Snap told us in writing on 24 Jul 2026 that both are calculated per month, so read them as $15,000 and $30,000 a month. Annual billing saves a flat $900 a year on both Accelerator and Standard — the same money, but 30 percent off the smaller plan against 15 percent off the larger one. Every tier carries a 15-day trial with no credit card, and in the monthly view each price is labelled 'Starting at'. Seller Snap confirmed to us in writing on 24 Jul 2026 that readers coming through our link get 10% off for their first three months; it runs through the link, there is no code to enter. Update: asked directly, Seller Snap confirmed by email on 24 July 2026 that the Starter and Accelerator revenue caps are calculated per month. Their pricing page still does not say so — we are passing on the vendor's answer, not something you can verify on the page yourself. One thing on the page has changed and it is not a price: a banner above the plans offers 'your first month for only $1 when you subscribe before 2026', a deadline that had already passed when we read it on 26 Aug 2026, so treat it as decoration rather than an offer until support confirms it.

tools.name: TextExpander
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-08-18 on the vendor's own pricing page; USD per user/month billed annually, excluding tax) The line-up was rebuilt since our July reading and it now starts at free. Free is $0 forever with no credit card, Pro $5 (billed annually at $60), Business $10 (billed annually at $120), Enterprise quoted. Annual billing is sold as two months free against paying monthly; the page does not print the monthly amounts next to the plans, so we do not quote them. The free plan is real but deliberately narrow: 5 active snippets out of an unlimited library, one snippet swap every two weeks, 3 teams, 5 team members and no snippet activity history at all. That history — what lets you see changes and restore deleted snippets — is 24 hours on Pro, 7 days on Business and unlimited only on Enterprise. Team members stay capped at 5 on Free and Pro; unlimited members start on Business, which is also the first tier with single sign-on (Google SSO on Business, all providers plus SCIM on Enterprise). A 30-day trial with full access to every feature and no credit card sits alongside the free plan. The page still carries an important pricing note for international customers, which we could not open on this reading, so treat the listed USD amounts as pre-tax.

tools.name: Tidio
tools.price_note:
(read 2026-08-24 on www.tidio.com/pricing/ with both billing columns clicked, and on www.tidio.com) The plan table opens on the annual column, so the first figures on the page are not what month-to-month costs. Starter is 24.17 a month billed annually against 29 paid monthly, Growth starts at 49.17 annually against 59 monthly, and the two stand-alone add-ons follow the same 20 percent step: the Lyro AI Agent from 32.50 annually against 39 monthly, Flows from 24.17 against 29. Plus is 300 a month in both columns and adds usage on top; Premium is contact-for-pricing. Tidio's own homepage quotes the higher, monthly number (“Paid plans from $29/mo, no surprise upgrades”), which makes the marketing page the more conservative of the two places you can read a price. The table rendered in euros on our reading while the same numerals appear with dollar signs on other retrievals of the same URL, so treat the figure rather than the symbol as the fact and confirm the currency at checkout.

What you pay is decided by three separate meters, not by the plan name. The free plan carries 50 billable conversations, 100 Flows visitors reached and 50 Lyro AI conversations, and the comparison table's own footnote makes that last allowance a lifetime one rather than a monthly one. Starter covers 100 billable conversations, Growth starts at 250 and the table caps it at 2,000, both with 10 seats and a 7-day free trial. Lyro conversations are upgradable from 50 to 1,000 and Flows visitors from 2,000 to 100,000. Two things the page does not say: what a conversation over the cap costs, and what the “discounted usage rates” next to Plus's “+ monthly usage” actually are. On Plus that unquoted rate is the whole variable, because the 300 is only the entry fee.

tools.name: TnC
tools.price_note:
(read 2026-08-25 on apps.shopify.com/terms-and-conditions-checkbox, listed as “TnC: Terms and Conditions Box”, and in the vendor's own pricing article on effectify.help) Every paid tier costs more than it did a day earlier: read on 24 August 2026 the ladder was $6.99, $9.99 and $12.99, and read again on 25 August 2026 the same three plans, carrying the same feature lists, showed $7.99, $12.99 and $14.99. Four plans on the listing, and the free one is not for you. Development Stores is free and carries every Pro feature, but the listing states it is for development and partner stores only and that payment will be activated on upgrade — so the “Free plan available” line at the top of the listing describes a partner sandbox rather than a free tier for a store that takes orders. Basic is $7.99 a month or $67.12 a year and covers the AI terms-and-conditions checkbox with support for Buy It Now and express checkout buttons. Advanced is $12.99 a month or $109.12 a year and adds the consent date logged into the order's details plus the ability to show the checkbox for specific countries and products. Pro is $14.99 a month or $125.92 a year and adds newsletter and contact forms, translation of the checkbox into multiple languages, the checkbox in Shopify POS and an AI-powered policies generator. Every paid tier carries a 7-day free trial, and the listing states charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days.

The vendor's own pricing article, last updated 25 August 2026, carries the same raised rates and lists a fifth plan the App Store listing does not: a Plus Plan at $19.99 a month or $167.92 a year, for Shopify Plus merchants only, adding “the ability to show the checkbox in the actual Checkout page of your store”. The Plus Plan is the one rate that did not move, so the gap between the top listed plan and the hidden one narrowed from $7 to $5. That article puts the annual saving at approximately 30% on every plan, which the listed annual rates match to the cent, and answers its own question “are there any hidden fees?” with “No. All pricing is transparent and listed above” — while being the only page where the Plus Plan appears at all. It also notes that uninstalling during an ongoing billing period still incurs that period's charge.

Developer Effective Apps, trading as Effectify, at 13 Max Nordau, Ashdod, Israel; the app launched on 2 December 2019, carries Shopify's Built for Shopify badge, and had 514 reviews at a 4.9 average at the time of writing. The listing names English, Vietnamese, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese (Brazil), Japanese and Chinese (Simplified) as supported languages.

tools.name: UENI
tools.price_note: (re-verified 2026-08-22, read in a live browser on their own US pricing page) A done-for-you website, now sold in four tiers rather than one. Every tier carries the same setup fee of $599, currently promoted at $79. Launch is $24.99/mo and covers a custom-designed site, domain and SSL, hosting, one professional email address and 30 days of done-for-you edits. Plus is $59.00/mo and adds unlimited done-for-you edits, four email addresses, advanced SEO, integrations such as live chat and lead forms, promotion on Google, Facebook and Instagram, and VIP phone support. Ecommerce is $99.00/mo and adds a full online store with abandoned cart recovery, social selling, subscriptions and courses, advanced bookings and deposits, automated sales tax and a loyalty programme. Growth is $124.99/mo and adds a dedicated VIP Growth Team, a custom marketing plan, monthly one-on-one sessions and 2,000 words of fresh content a month. A yearly toggle advertises about 17% off: our August capture records $20.83 a month ($249.90 billed annually) on Launch and $49.17 ($590) on Plus, with two-year rates of $18.74 ($449.82) and $44.25 ($1,062). Transaction fees are 0% on every tier and there is a 30-day money-back guarantee.

tools.name: Unleashed Software
tools.price_note: (prices read 2026-08-17 on unleashedsoftware.com/pricing) Two bundles, in USD and excluding tax. Onboarding is a one-off fee on top: $449 self-service, $799 standard, $5,549 full. Optional modules start at $119 a month for Advanced Inventory Manager, $262 for Marketing Accelerator and $450 for CRM.
